uncertain.text: ne de ce crime, iaçoit que l'empereur la face capitale {k}.
uncertain.note: the mark after marker {k} is a round blob on the baseline, read as a period; at 8x it could also be a tailless comma. Sense would favour a comma.

uncertain.text: tout eſtre verifié, cõcluoit a l'encontre.
uncertain.note: two doubts on this line: (a) the accent on 'verifié' is a small wedge, acute is the likely reading but grave 'verifiè' is possible; (b) the line ends with a clear round dot (period) mid-sentence where a hyphen or comma would be expected before 'dudit'. Transcribed as printed.
abbreviated citation; 'nesem' has a round s and no clear suspension mark, the leading 'l' carries no visible period. Could be 'l. ſi neceſſ.' expanded differently.

the line-initial siglum is a long ſ with a small round s beside it (no crossbars, so not 'ff'; the second stroke has no descender, so not 'ſſ'). Almost certainly the Digest siglum. It sits at the key column but has no marker in the body, so it is treated as a continuation line of note l, not a key.
'liberto' is broken across lines and the break is printed as a round dot ('li.' / 'berto.'), not a hyphen. Transcribed as printed.
first letter read as 'c' (matching the 'c' of 'ceſte' two lines down) giving 'ch.' = chapitre, the usual citation of Benedicti on cap. Raynutius; at this size it could be read as 'eh.'
the -que sign after 'itaq' is printed as a roman semicolon, not the 3-shaped ꝫ, so transcribed ';'.
digits read as 1-5-9 in old-style figures; the 5 is worn.

uncertain.text: pour ſon intereſt {a}. & par ainſi ne peut conclure à peine
uncertain.note: 'par ainſi' is set tight as one token in the print; split per the word-division rule.
